note: Delhi's flagship water bodies: the multi-dynasty hydraulic chain (hauz, baoli, fortress cisterns) plus the modern lakes that anchor restoration stories. Coordinates are monument/landmark positions from OSM and ASI listings, not survey-grade. Confidence grades: A = well-documented + site verified in multiple sources; B = well-documented, minor figure spread across sources; C = figures contested or in flux.

bodies.name: Hauz Khas tank
bodies.builder: Alauddin Khalji; restored by Firuz Shah Tughlaq
bodies.feed: Historically monsoon runoff from the Aravalli slopes; today treated-effluent + stormwater makeup via DDA
bodies.status: Wet and publicly accessible inside the Hauz Khas Complex; a fragment of the original ~50 ha royal tank, revived with recycled water after decades dry.
bodies.cultural_note: The 'royal tank' that watered Siri Fort; Firuz Shah's madrasa and tomb stand on its bund - the most legible piece of Sultanate waterworks in India.
bodies.location_basis: ASI-protected Hauz Khas Complex, South Delhi

bodies.name: Hauz-i-Shamsi
bodies.status: Wet; shrunken from its original extent, water quality poor, but continuously in ritual use for nearly 800 years (the annual Phoolwalon-ki-Sair procession starts here).
bodies.cultural_note: Delhi's oldest surviving royal reservoir; the Jahaz Mahal 'ship palace' on its bank appears to float at high water.

bodies.name: Agrasen ki Baoli
bodies.era: 14th century (rebuilt on a possibly older site)
bodies.builder: Attributed to the Agrawal community (legendary attribution to Maharaja Agrasen)
bodies.feed: Groundwater (60 m x 15 m stepwell, 108 steps, three tiers)
bodies.status: Dry at the lower tiers most of the year; ASI-protected and heavily visited - the CBD's incongruous medieval stepwell.
bodies.cultural_note: The most famous of Delhi's baolis, steps from Connaught Place; a barometer of the central ridge aquifer - its historic water levels are the citable proof of how far the water table has fallen.
bodies.location_basis: Hailey Road, off Connaught Place (ASI monument)

bodies.name: Rajon ki Baoli
bodies.status: Restored (ASI + World Monuments Fund conservation, completed 2024-25); holds water seasonally.
bodies.cultural_note: The grandest of the Mehrauli stepwells - four tiers with arcaded galleries; 'of the masons' (raj = mason), not 'of kings'.

bodies.name: Nizamuddin Baoli (Baoli of Hazrat Nizamuddin Auliya)
bodies.feed: Live springs - one of the only Delhi baolis still spring-fed
bodies.status: Restored by AKTC (2008-2011, structural rescue after a 2008 collapse) within the Nizamuddin renewal; in daily ritual use at the dargah.
bodies.cultural_note: Legend has the saint's workers building it by night against Tughlaq prohibition - Delhi's most storied and most alive water monument.

bodies.name: Tughlaqabad fort cisterns & baolis
bodies.feed: Rainwater harvesting into rock-cut cisterns + up to seven baolis within the fort circuit
bodies.status: Ruined but legible; ASI-protected. The fort's southern reservoir bund survives as a causeway.
bodies.cultural_note: A 14th-century city designed around stored rainwater on a waterless ridge - the engineering answer to why the capital kept moving toward the Yamuna.

bodies.name: Sanjay Lake
bodies.builder: Delhi Development Authority (from abandoned brick-kiln pits)
bodies.feed: Stormwater + regulated Yamuna-linked inflow; desilting + STP-makeup under the current rejuvenation
bodies.status: Under active DDA rejuvenation (desilting ~60% reported 2025; 53 ML storage target); East Delhi's principal lake-park.
bodies.cultural_note: Trilokpuri's engineered lake - proof that Delhi can create water bodies, not only lose them.

bodies.name: Bhalswa Lake
bodies.feed: Historically Yamuna flood connection; now sewage-stressed catchment inflow
bodies.status: Down from ~58 ha to ~34 ha; ~50 t/day of dairy-colony waste cited in its catchment; DDA clean-up announced 2025 - Delhi's hardest lake-restoration test.
bodies.cultural_note: A natural river relic ringed by the city's most infamous landfill - the north Delhi mirror of the floodplain's decline.
bodies.location_basis: Bhalswa, north-west Delhi (adjacent to the landfill)

bodies.name: Najafgarh Jheel (remnant)
bodies.era: Natural (terminal lake of the Sahibi river)
bodies.feed: Sahibi/Najafgarh drain backflow + monsoon runoff from Delhi and Gurugram
bodies.status: ~7 sq km remnant of a ~226 sq km lake; the largest water body in the NCT today (601 ha in the OSM layer). Wetland notification stuck between Delhi and Haryana since INTACH's 2014 petition; NGT-ordered Environment Management Plans exist on both sides.
bodies.cultural_note: Winter habitat for tens of thousands of waterbirds including flamingos and sarus cranes - a Ramsar-grade site administered as a boundary dispute.
bodies.location_basis: Delhi-Haryana border, south-west Delhi (matches the 601-ha polygon in delhi-water-bodies-current.geojson)

bodies.name: Yamuna Biodiversity Park wetlands
bodies.builder: DDA + CEMDE (Delhi University), led by Prof. C.R. Babu / Dr. Faiyaz Khudsar
bodies.feed: Rain + regulated Yamuna flood connection (Phase II active floodplain)
bodies.status: Functioning restored wetland mosaic at Wazirabad; DDA credits its park network with recharging ~1 lakh million gallons since 2021.
bodies.cultural_note: The standing existence-proof for floodplain restoration in the same city that builds on its floodplain.
bodies.location_basis: Wazirabad village, near the Outer Ring Road

bodies.name: Neela Hauz
bodies.builder: DDA restoration with IIT-Delhi + citizen groups (constructed-wetland treatment)
bodies.feed: Stormwater treated through a constructed wetland before entering the lake
bodies.status: Restored and designated a biodiversity area - Delhi's cleanest small-lake success story.
bodies.cultural_note: The 'blue tank' below Sanjay Van: a citizen-litigated restoration that actually finished.
bodies.location_basis: Aruna Asaf Ali Marg, below Sanjay Van, South Delhi

bodies.name: Purana Qila moat
bodies.feed: Historically Yamuna-connected; now maintained with recycled water after 2023-24 restoration
bodies.status: Wet, boating restored; the fort's western moat was revived as part of the ASI + Sabhyata Foundation redevelopment.
bodies.cultural_note: The one place in Delhi where you can still see a Yamuna-fed fortification waterline - the river's old right bank runs beside the fort.
